title: Provision S3 Bucket
scenario: Your platform team needs S3 Bucket for durable object storage for application assets. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_s3_bucket.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_s3_bucket resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_s3_bucket.

hints.why: S3 is usually the first shared service in an AWS configuration. Bucket settings, versioning, encryption and public-access blocks are common review findings.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_s3_bucket" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_s3_bucket. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use S3 when you need durable object storage for assets, logs, backups or static content, and lock down access from the start.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_s3_bucket" "this"`. Use this code shape: bucket; tags; force_destroy. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.bucket_name`, `var.project_name`, `var.environment`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
